Clinical context helps explain definite-zone p-tau217 discordance

Among 706 Mayo Clinic patients with plasma p-tau217 outside the intermediate zone and confirmatory amyloid PET and/or CSF, 60 (8.5%) were discordant: false negatives were more common than false positives (5.6% vs 2.8%; p=0.007), with disease stage, kidney function, body mass index and obstructive sleep apnea associated with discordance patterns.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217AmyloidBiological confirmation

Added October 2, 2026 · DOI:10.1212/WNL.0000000000218591; PMID:42821845

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Definite-zone p-tau217 results agreed with established amyloid measures in most patients, but discordance was not random. False negatives clustered with milder clinical stage, higher body mass index, better kidney function and obstructive sleep apnea; false positives clustered with older age, lower kidney function and more advanced impairment. These are signals for confirmatory testing and contextual interpretation, not post hoc permission to relabel a discordant result or use the associations as correction factors.

Study design

Investigators retrospectively identified 706 Mayo Clinic patients whose plasma p-tau217 was definitely positive (>0.324 pg/mL) or definitely negative (<0.186 pg/mL) and who had an amyloid PET and/or CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 result. They classified plasma results as true positive, true negative, false positive or false negative against the established biomarker result and modeled demographic, clinical, comorbidity and laboratory factors associated with discordance.

Key quantitative results

  • Sixty of 706 patients (8.5%) had discordant results. False negatives occurred in 5.6% and false positives in 2.8% (p=0.007). Across both discordance types, older age was associated with discordance (OR 1.61 per decade; 95% CI 1.23–2.14), as was obstructive sleep apnea (OR 1.94; 95% CI 1.08–3.49).
  • Compared with true positives, false negatives had higher MMSE scores (OR 1.20 per point), more obstructive sleep apnea (OR 2.01), higher body mass index (OR 1.11 per kg/m²) and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR 1.33 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m²). Age-adjusted analyses retained body mass index (OR 1.14), estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR 1.63) and earlier Clinical Dementia Rating stage as associations.
  • Compared with true negatives, false positives were associated with older age (OR 2.37 per decade), thyroid disease (OR 4.41), lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR 0.48 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m²) and more advanced Clinical Dementia Rating stage. In age-adjusted analyses, estimated glomerular filtration rate remained associated (OR 0.54), while CDR ≥1 carried OR 11.11 versus CDR 0 and OR 4.55 versus CDR 0.5.

What changed

An October 1 Neurology report quantifies the residual discordance within definite plasma p-tau217 zones and identifies clinical patterns that can guide when a seemingly definitive result still warrants adjudication with PET, CSF or broader diagnostic evaluation.

Strength of evidence

Moderate clinical-validity and interpretation evidence from a 706-patient specialty-center cohort with established-biomarker comparators. Associations are observational, several subgroups are small, the reference standard combines PET and CSF, and the public abstract does not establish prospective decision impact or transportability to other assays and settings.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A definite plasma result should be interpreted alongside clinical stage and kidney function, with attention to obesity and obstructive sleep apnea when the phenotype and biomarker disagree. The findings support targeted confirmation rather than automatic acceptance or mathematical adjustment of the plasma value.

Field medical relevance

Directly relevant to blood-biomarker triage, discordant-result workups, specialty referral, pretest counseling and communication about why two-cutoff algorithms reduce but do not eliminate uncertainty.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The study used an assay-specific two-cutoff plasma p-tau217 workflow, with definite negative below 0.186 pg/mL and definite positive above 0.324 pg/mL. The public abstract does not name the assay platform; the cutoffs and associations should not be transferred to other products, matrices or workflows without validation.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization, availability, guideline or coverage change occurred. The study may improve selection for confirmatory testing, but payer requirements and product-specific intended uses remain unchanged.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does 8.5% mean the test was only 91.5% accurate?
Not necessarily. The cohort included only definite-zone plasma results with PET and/or CSF confirmation, and the analysis focused on discordance rather than a population-screening accuracy estimate. Prevalence, referral patterns and the combined reference standard affect the observed proportion.
Should kidney function or body mass index be used to correct p-tau217 values?
No correction equation was validated. These variables identify contexts in which discordance was more likely and may justify confirmation; they do not establish a new adjusted cutoff.
Did the study establish clinical utility?
No. It supports clinical validity and contextual interpretation but did not test whether using these factors improves decisions, treatment eligibility, outcomes, safety or cost.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Retrospective specialty-center cohort
  • Observational associations cannot establish why discordance occurred
  • Amyloid PET and CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 were combined as the established-biomarker reference
  • Only 60 discordant cases, with smaller false-positive and false-negative subgroups
  • Public abstract does not name the assay platform or report external validation
  • No prospective decision-impact, treatment-access or patient-outcome evaluation

Primary source · DOI · PubMed record

Shir D, Algeciras-Schimnich A, Piura YD, et al. Clinical factors associated with discordant plasma P-Tau217 and established Alzheimer disease biomarkers. Neurology. Published online October 1, 2026. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000218591.
